question: Coromandel Coast gets most of its rain during the winter season because:

options.text: the winds from the Indian Ocean are obstructed by the Eastern Ghats
the cyclones from the Indian Ocean are obstructed by the Western Ghats
the Northeast monsoons pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and these winds are obstructed by the Eastern Ghats
the Northwest monsoons pick up moisture from the Arabian Sea and these winds are obstructed by the Western Ghats

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Coromandel Coast receive more rainfall in the retreating monsoon season than the normal rainy season.
 
• The retreating monsoon occurs when the winds become weaker and start to retreat back from the skies of North India to the Bay of Bengal. 
 
• As a result, the skies become clearer and clouds disappear. 
 
• The weather becomes extremely hot and humid because of which cyclones start emerging in the Bay of Bengal because of which the coast along the Bay of Bengal receives heavy rainfall. 
 
• It takes three months starting in mid-November and till January.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• November to January is also the period of tropical cyclones.
 
• This period is also referred to as northeast monsoon or winter monsoon as the northeastern states also receive rainfall during this time.
